title: India Transition Factbook 2026 | BloombergNEF
gist: BloombergNEF's India Transition Factbook finds India was the second-largest solar and wind market in 2025, passed 50% non-fossil capacity five years early, and could cut energy imports from 5.3% to 3.1% of GDP by 2035. It also flags cheap green ammonia exports, an EV shortfall versus 2030 targets, and data center demand rising from 11 TWh to 636 TWh by 2050.

insights.claim: India was the second-largest market for annual solar and wind capacity additions in 2025 behind only China, and BNEF expects it to stay the second-largest solar market for the foreseeable future on rising power demand and lower equipment prices.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: India is the durable number-two demand pool for solar equipment and developers outside China.
insights.locator: India is a global leader in clean power adoption

insights.claim: Non-fossil technologies made up 80% of new generation capacity added to India's grid over the last decade and supplied one-third of electricity demand in the first seven months of 2026, yet coal still provided the majority of power.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: Capacity share far outruns generation share, so coal remains the incumbent baseline and displacement is gradual.
insights.locator: Renewables are starting to cut into coal's share

insights.claim: The non-fossil share of India's installed grid capacity crossed 50% in 2025, five years ahead of the 2022 NDC target, and BNEF projects it will exceed 60% in 2028, seven years ahead of the revised NDC.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: India repeatedly beats its own climate targets on capacity, lowering policy-risk for renewable build-out assumptions.
insights.locator: India has achieved a key clean power capacity goal early

insights.claim: India's revised NDC target of a 47% cut in GDP emissions intensity by 2035 from 2005 levels is achievable under BNEF's base-case scenario.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: The headline climate goal needs no extra policy push in the base case, reducing the odds of disruptive new mandates.
insights.locator: Meeting India's 2035 emissions-intensity goal is achievable

insights.claim: Investors committed $72 billion to India's energy transition in 2025, about 1.7% of GDP, making it the fifth-largest transition investment market.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: Sizeable but still modest relative to GDP, leaving room for growth in financing flows.
insights.locator: India is the fifth-largest market for energy-transition investment

insights.claim: India's wind and solar sectors alone will need $123 billion to $163 billion of capital through 2030 in real 2025 dollars, well above the 2025 pace of total transition investment.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: Implies a multi-year financing pipeline for developers, lenders and equipment suppliers.
insights.locator: India's wind and solar sectors alone will have capital requirements

insights.claim: India plans transmission infrastructure by Q1 2032 to connect 336 GW of renewable capacity, roughly twice the UK's existing grid capacity, making it the fourth-largest grid investment market.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: Grid build is the enabling bottleneck, so transmission and equipment suppliers are a second-order beneficiary of the renewables push.
insights.locator: India is the world's fourth-largest market for grid investment

insights.claim: In an economics-led shift without new supportive policy, BNEF models India's energy imports falling from 5.3% of GDP in 2025 to 3.1% in 2035 and 1.5% by mid-century.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: Cheaper clean power lowers the structural oil-import and current-account burden, a macro positive for India.
insights.locator: The transition to lower-carbon energy sources can strengthen India's energy security

insights.claim: Higher fuel costs stemming from the conflict in the Persian Gulf could improve EV economics in India.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: Oil-price shocks act as a demand catalyst for Indian EVs.
insights.locator: Electric vehicle sales are up but India is far from hitting

insights.claim: Indian firms signed binding contracts in the first four months of 2026 for 0.3 million tonnes a year of clean hydrogen, including exports as green ammonia, more than firms in any other country, lifting India to third globally in cumulative contracted volumes.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: India is converting hydrogen ambition into contracted offtake, unlike many announced projects elsewhere.
insights.locator: India's hydrogen ambitions are bearing fruit

insights.claim: India produces some of the world's cheapest green ammonia thanks to low-cost clean power, generous subsidies and competitive auctions, and has signed three major binding offtake deals to export more than 1 million tonnes a year.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: Low-cost renewables plus auctions give India a cost edge in exportable green molecules.
insights.locator: The country's growth has been supported by its ability

insights.claim: India targets EVs at 80% of two- and three-wheeler sales, 70% of commercial vehicles and 30% of private cars by 2030, but BNEF modeling says it will miss most of these, with three-wheelers the exception.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: Official targets overstate near-term EV volumes for cars, commercial vehicles and two-wheelers, so forecasts should be haircut.
insights.locator: Electric vehicle sales are up but India is far from hitting

insights.claim: Lower total cost of ownership, greater model availability and a sustained policy push are boosting Indian EV sales, though further measures will be needed to hit all 2030 targets.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: Adoption is economics-driven, which makes growth more resilient to subsidy changes.
insights.locator: Lower total cost of ownership, greater model availability

insights.claim: Data center power demand in India could rise from 11 TWh in 2025 to 636 TWh by 2050, about 11% of the country's electricity consumption, a roughly 58-fold increase.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: A major new demand driver for power generation and grid assets over the coming decades.
insights.locator: Flexible power procurement can support greener data center growth

insights.claim: With coal supplying about 68% of India's electricity, data centers on standard grid supply are exposed to carbon-intensive power and can reduce this through third-party contracts, captive and group-captive projects, onsite solar and power exchanges.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: Corporate renewable procurement structures are a growth niche tied to data center demand.
insights.locator: This leaves data centers reliant on standard grid supply
